questions.question: You are counting by 2s on a number line. You are at 6. What number do you land on next?
questions.explain: Counting by 2s means you add 2 each time, so after 6 you say 8. The trap is slipping back to counting by 1 and saying 7.

questions.question: You are counting by 5s on a number line. You are at 5. What number do you land on next?
questions.explain: Counting by 5s means you add 5 each time, so after 5 you say 10. Watch out for mixing in the 2s step and landing on 7.

questions.question: Mia jumps rope and points to numbers on a hundred chart. She counts by 5s for 3 jumps. What number does she point to last?
questions.explain: Her jumps land on 5, 10, 15. The last number is 15. The trap is counting by 1s or by 2s instead of 5s.

questions.question: Liam has 4 pairs of shoes. He traces them on a hundred chart, counting by 2s. What number does he reach?
questions.explain: One pair is 2: 2, 4, 6, 8. Four pairs get him to 8. Watch for counting by 1s and stopping at 5.

questions.question: A bus driver counts stops on a chart, saying 5 for each stop. After 4 stops, what number does he say?
questions.explain: He says 5, 10, 15, 20. After 4 stops the number is 20. Easy to mix up and count by 2s, getting 11.

questions.question: Look at this row: 2, 4, 6, __, 10, 12. What number goes in the blank?
questions.explain: The step is 2, so after 6 comes 8. If you add 1 instead you get 7, and if you add 3 you get 9.

questions.question: Ben has 6 buttons. His sister gives him 4 more. He counts all of them by 2s. What is the last number he says?
questions.explain: 6 plus 4 is 10 buttons. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The last number is 10. Watch for counting by 1s and stopping at 6.

questions.question: Look at this row: 5, __, 15, 20. What number goes in the blank?
questions.explain: The step is 5, so after 5 comes 10. If you count by 1s you get 6, and if you count by 2s you get 7.

questions.question: Zoe writes: 2, 4, 6, 7, 8. What went wrong?
options: She used a wrong step all along.
She gave the count, not the total.
She missed one at the very start.
questions.explain: Her first three numbers (2, 4, 6) are right, but 7 and 8 mean she switched to counting by 1s. The step changed in the middle.

questions.question: You are counting by 5s on a number line. You start at 0 and make 4 jumps. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. Four jumps of 5 land on 20. A common trap is to say the number of jumps (4) instead of the total.

questions.question: You are counting by 2s on a number line. You start at 0 and make 5 jumps. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Five jumps of 2 land on 10. Watch out for slipping to +1 in the middle, like 2, 4, 5, 6, 7.

questions.question: You are counting by 5s on a number line. You start at 0 and make 3 jumps. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. Three jumps of 5 land on 15. A common mistake is to count by 2s instead and get 6.

questions.question: You are counting by 2s on a number line. You start at 0 and make 7 jumps. What number do you land on?
questions.explain: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Seven jumps of 2 land on 14. Be careful not to add 1 in the middle, like 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

questions.question: Lily has 2 hands with 5 fingers each. She counts by 5s from 0, one number per hand. What number does she say last?
questions.explain: Say 5 for the first hand and 10 for the second. The total is 10, not the number of hands (2).

questions.question: Max has 6 pairs of socks. He counts them by 2s from 0, one number per pair. What number does he say last?
questions.explain: Say 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 for each pair. The last number is 12. A common trap is to count by 3s instead and get 18.

questions.question: A snail crawls 2 cm each step. It takes 9 steps and counts by 2s from 0. What number does it say last?
questions.explain: Say 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 for each step. The last number is 18. Be careful not to slip to +1 partway through the count.

questions.question: A cat has 5 toe-lines on each of its 4 paws. It counts by 5s from 0, one number per paw. What number does it say last?
questions.explain: Say 5, 10, 15, 20 for each paw. The last number is 20. A common mistake is to say the number of paws (4) instead of the total.
